newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
DECKS CLEARED FOR LALOO'S ARREST

The Central Bureau of Investigations (CBI) asked its joint director to arrest former Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav in a fodder scam case as his anticipatory bail plea was rejected by the Supreme Court. But Laloo Yadav Tuesday night said he would surrender before the special court on Wednesday. The CBI director asked his joint director to take utmost care and precaution while executing the arrest warrants in accordance with the law, sources said. Personnel of the Rapid Action Force were deployed along a one kilometer stretch of the road leading to Laloo Yadav's home from the CBI office.
The Economic Times
INDIA OFFERS TO OPEN UP FINANCIAL SERVICES MARKET
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram offered to open up the financial services market if other countries made improved offers to India in accessing their markets.
BB+ RATING FOR YANKEE BONDS

International credit rating agency Standard and Poors assigned a BB+ rating to the proposed $150 million Yankee bond offering of the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI). The bonds are issued under the ICICI's existing $500 million medium term note programme. The Standard and Poors said the outlook for the bonds was stable. The rating reflects the company's strong market franchise, sound capitalisation and good profitability, it said.
BOURSE REGULATOR PLANS JOINT OFFER OF SECURITIES

Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is exploring the possibility of joint offer of securities by Indian companies in the local and international markets. The move is expected to revive the sagging Indian capital markets.
INDUSTRIAL CREDIT AND INVESTMENT FIRM TO BE A BANK

The ICICI has decided to become a commercial bank in 18 months. It discussed the specific issues to be addressed to facilitate the conversion with the Reserve Bank. The two are expected to begin formal discussions on the issues within a few months.
Financial Express
BANK OF INDIA TO CUT PRIME LENDING RATE

The Bank of India is planning to slash its prime lending rate and the deposit rates across all maturities. The Bombay-based bank has decided to privately place about 15 billion rupees worth of subordinated debt between July and September this fiscal year. With this, the state-owned bank's capital adequacy ratio which is now 10.26 percent will go up substantially.
AIR LIQUIDE, SAKATA HIKE STAKE IN INDIAN VENTURES

Air Liquide of France and Sakata Inx Corporation of Japan have substantially hiked equity stakes in their joint ventures in India. This was approved by the government. Air Liquide acquired an additional 17 percent stake in the Air Liquide North India rising its total stake in the company to 93 percent. The remaining seven percent will be held by Indian businesspeople. The equity base is being expanded to further modernise and expand the plant. Sakata Inx hiked its equity holding in Montari Sakata Inx to 75 percent from 30 percent.
SIX BLN RUPEE ISSUE BY INDUSTRIAL CREDIT FIRM

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) will tap the retail debt market with a six billion rupee public issue. The issue will have a core size of three billion rupees and a greenshoe option of another three billion rupees. It is expected to hit the market in September.
Business Standard
FIAT, PEUGEOT LIKELY TO FORGE ALLIANCE IN INDIA
Italian auto major Fiat and its French rival Peugeot are likely to strike a strategic alliance in India by Peugeot sharing its manufacturing facility with Fiat to produce Fiat's Palio car in India.
The Observer
IMPORT OF FABRICS, MADE-UPS LIKELY TO BE FREED

India plans to remove import restrictions on fabrics and made-ups from 1998 as part of her phase out package on removing quantitive restrictions on imports. These will be put on the Open General Licence list. At present textile items could be imported only under the Special Import Licence which many countries consider as an import restriction. India is a leading textiles exporter to the United States and the European Union. Both the United states and the European Union were pressurising India to allow imports of textile products without linking them to any kind of import licence.
NO SUBSIDY ON NAPHTHA
The ministries of power and petroleum said there would be no subsidy on liquid fuel for power projects. But the Power Ministry will ensure fuel linkages for specified projects.
